title: MATH GAOKAO - 412
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the average rate of change of a polynomial function over a closed interval.
questions.question: For the function \(f(x)=x^2+2x\), find its average rate of change on the interval \([1,3]\).
questions.explanation: The average rate of change is \(\frac{f(3)-f(1)}{3-1}\). Now \(f(3)=9+6=15\) and \(f(1)=1+2=3\), so the average rate of change is \(\frac{15-3}{2}=6\).
questions.hint: Use the formula for average rate of change: \(\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the instantaneous rate of change of a quadratic function at a given point.
questions.question: For \(f(x)=3x^2-4x+1\), what is the instantaneous rate of change at \(x=2\)?
questions.explanation: The instantaneous rate of change is given by the derivative \(f'(x)=6x-4\). Substituting \(x=2\), we get \(f'(2)=6(2)-4=8\).
questions.hint: Differentiate the function first, then evaluate the derivative at the given value of \(x\).

questions.concept: Velocity as a Rate of Change
questions.learningObjective: Find the velocity of an object at a given time from its position function.
questions.question: A car moves along a straight road so that its position measured from the starting point after \(t\) seconds is \(s(t)=2t^3-9t^2+12t\) meters. What is its velocity at \(t=2\) seconds?
questions.explanation:
Velocity is the derivative of position: \(s'(t)=6t^2-18t+12\). At \(t=2\), \[
\begin{aligned}
s'(2)&=6(4)-18(2)+12 \\
&=24-36+12 \\
&=0
\end{aligned}
\]. Thus the velocity is \(0\text{ m}\text{/s}\).
questions.hint: Differentiate the position function with respect to time to obtain the velocity function.

questions.learningObjective: Use related rates to find the rate of change of a sphere's surface area.
questions.question: A spherical balloon is inflated so that its radius increases at \(0.5\text{ cm}\text{/s}\). At the instant the radius is \(10\text{ cm}\), at what rate is its surface area increasing? Use \(S=4\pi r^2\).
questions.explanation: Differentiate \(S=4\pi r^2\) with respect to time: \(\frac{dS}{dt}=8\pi r\frac{dr}{dt}\). Substituting \(r=10\) and \(\frac{dr}{dt}=0.5\), we get \(\frac{dS}{dt}=8\pi(10)(0.5)=40\pi\text{ cm}^2\text{/s}\).
questions.hint: Differentiate the surface area formula with respect to time and use the given rate of change of the radius.

questions.concept: Rate of Change of an Exponential Model
questions.learningObjective: Find the initial rate of change of an exponential population model.
questions.question: A population is modeled by \(P(t)=500e^{0.02t}\), where \(t\) is measured in years. What is the rate of change of the population at \(t=0\)?
questions.hint: Differentiate the exponential function using the chain rule, then evaluate at \(t=0\).

questions.concept: Marginal Cost as a Rate of Change
questions.learningObjective: Compute the marginal cost from a cubic cost function at a given production level.
questions.question: The cost of producing \(x\) units of a product is \(C(x)=0.01x^3-0.3x^2+5x+100\text{ yuan}\). What is the marginal cost when \(x=20\)?
questions.explanation:
Marginal cost is \(C'(x)\). Differentiate: \(C'(x)=0.03x^2-0.6x+5\). At \(x=20\), \[
\begin{aligned}
C'(20)&=0.03(400)-0.6(20)+5 \\
&=12-12+5 \\
&=5
\end{aligned}
\]. Thus the marginal cost is \(5\text{ yuan}\) per unit.
questions.hint: Find the derivative of the cost function and evaluate it at the given production level.

questions.concept: Related Rates in a Ladder Problem
questions.learningObjective: Determine the speed of a sliding ladder using related rates.
questions.question: A \(5\text{ m}\) ladder rests against a vertical wall. The bottom of the ladder is pulled away from the wall at \(1\text{ m}\text{/s}\). When the bottom is \(3\text{ m}\) from the wall, how fast is the top of the ladder sliding down?
questions.explanation: Let \(x\) be the distance from the wall to the bottom of the ladder and \(y\) be the height of the top. Then \(x^2+y^2=25\). When \(x=3\), \(y=4\). Differentiating gives \(2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt}=0\). Since \(\frac{dx}{dt}=1\), we get \(2(3)(1)+2(4)\frac{dy}{dt}=0\), so \(\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac{3}{4}\). The top slides down at \(\frac{3}{4}\text{ m}\text{/s}\).
questions.hint: Use the Pythagorean relation between the distances and differentiate both sides with respect to time.

questions.concept: Average Speed Over Two Equal Distances
questions.learningObjective: Calculate average speed when different speeds are used over equal distances.
questions.question: A cyclist covers the first half of the total distance of a trip at \(30\text{ km}\text{/h}\) and the second half at \(60\text{ km}\text{/h}\). What is the average speed for the entire trip?
questions.hint: Average speed is total distance divided by total time, not the arithmetic mean of the two speeds.

questions.concept: Related Rates in a Conical Tank
questions.learningObjective: Find the rate of change of water volume in a draining conical tank.
questions.question: Water drains from an inverted right circular conical tank, with its vertex at the bottom, whose top radius is \(2\text{ m}\) and whose height is \(4\text{ m}\). When the water depth is \(4\text{ m}\), the water level is falling at \(0.1\text{ m}\text{/min}\). At what rate is the volume of water decreasing at that instant?
questions.hint: Express the radius in terms of the water depth using similar triangles before differentiating the volume formula.

questions.concept: Velocity and Acceleration as Rates of Change
questions.learningObjective: Find the velocity of a particle when its acceleration is zero.
questions.question: A particle moves along a straight line so that its position at time \(t\) is \(s(t)=t^3-6t^2+9t+1\). Find the velocity of the particle when its acceleration is zero.
questions.explanation:
Velocity is \(s'(t)=3t^2-12t+9\), and acceleration is \(s''(t)=6t-12\). Setting acceleration equal to zero gives \(6t-12=0\), so \(t=2\). Then \[
\begin{aligned}
s'(2)&=3(4)-12(2)+9 \\
&=12-24+9 \\
&=-3
\end{aligned}
\]. Thus the velocity is \(-3\).
questions.hint: Differentiate the position function twice to obtain velocity and acceleration, then set acceleration equal to zero.
